title: Mbah presents Enugu scorecard and outlines next development priorities
excerpt: At a public account-giving event in Enugu, Governor Peter Mbah highlighted security, roads, education, health and transport, while acknowledging that some communities are still waiting for promised improvements.
body: Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah presented an account of his administration’s work at a town-hall event at Godfrey Okoye University this week, describing progress in security, road construction, aviation, education, healthcare, tourism and agriculture. The gathering brought together academics, students, business owners, civil society groups and other residents. Mbah said his government was working to restore Enugu’s appeal as a place to live, work, invest and visit.

Among the initiatives he cited were the 260 Smart Green Schools planned for wards across the state, new transport arrangements, road projects and the development of Enugu Air. He also restated a long-term ambition to expand the state economy from an estimated US$4.4 billion to US$30 billion. These figures and progress claims were presented by the governor and have not been independently audited as part of the event.

Mbah acknowledged that some communities are still waiting for roads to be completed, public facilities to become fully operational or new opportunities to reach them. He said the administration would continue listening to concerns and described citizen scrutiny as part of public accountability. The scorecard places the government’s development priorities on record; residents will be able to assess them against projects completed, services delivered and the needs that remain unmet.

title: Uzodimma to appeal ruling that awards Imo West APC ticket to Okorocha
excerpt: A Federal High Court ordered the APC to recognise Rochas Okorocha as its Imo West senatorial candidate. Governor Hope Uzodimma’s camp says it will challenge the decision.
body: The contest for the All Progressives Congress ticket in Imo West has moved into a new phase after a Federal High Court in Abuja ruled that former governor Rochas Okorocha won the party’s May 2026 senatorial primary. Justice Obiora Egwuatu ordered the party to forward Okorocha’s name to the Independent National Electoral Commission and restrained Governor Hope Uzodimma from presenting himself as the party’s nominee for the January 2027 election.

The case centred on conflicting accounts of the primary and documents submitted to support the candidates’ claims. The judge said the evidence before the court established that Okorocha received the winning votes and found problems with the records used to support Uzodimma’s nomination. The APC and INEC had disputed Okorocha’s account during the proceedings.

Uzodimma’s camp has said it will challenge the judgment at the Court of Appeal. The Imo APC chapter has also maintained that the governor remains its candidate while it reviews the decision. The dispute is therefore not politically settled: the High Court has issued its order, but an appeal could affect the final outcome. The case is one of several early contests shaping the run-up to Nigeria’s 2027 elections.

title: Dakar prepares to open Africa’s first Olympic event
excerpt: The Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games are set to begin on Saturday, bringing nearly 2,700 young athletes from 204 national Olympic committees to Senegal.
body: Senegal is preparing to host the opening of the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games on Saturday, marking the first time an Olympic sporting event has been staged on African soil. Organisers expect nearly 2,700 athletes aged 14 to 17, representing 204 national Olympic committees, to take part. The programme is scheduled to run through November 13.

The Games were originally planned for 2022 but were postponed during the COVID-19 pandemic. International Olympic Committee President Kirsty Coventry visited the athletes’ village and venues ahead of the opening and said preparations were ready to proceed. Organisers have reported last-minute energy and weather challenges, while more than 6,000 volunteers are supporting event operations.

The event is being watched as both a competition and a test of the legacy major sports events can leave. Facilities, trained staff and event-management experience could support future competitions in the region, but that benefit depends on how well venues are maintained and used after the closing ceremony. South Africa has also named Durban as its candidate city for a possible 2036 or 2040 Summer Olympics, keeping Africa’s place in global sports hosting in focus.

title: Spain mourns victims as investigators examine deadly train collision
excerpt: At least 68 people have died after two high-speed trains collided in Toledo province. Authorities are investigating the circumstances and Spain has begun three days of national mourning.
body: Spain has begun three days of national mourning after a collision between two high-speed trains in Toledo province killed at least 68 people and injured many others. The crash happened on Wednesday when a Renfe train struck an Iryo train that was stopped on the track. Emergency teams continued searching damaged carriages and supporting survivors as rail services on the affected route were disrupted.

Transport Minister Óscar Puente said an equipment failure had brought trains to a stop and that a subsequent instruction from the central control centre allowed the Renfe train to resume its journey. He described that instruction as inexplicable. Those are preliminary statements, not a final finding: investigators are examining the sequence of communications, rail systems and decisions that preceded the impact.

The disaster has renewed questions about safety on Spain’s high-speed network, particularly because it is the country’s second deadly rail collision this year. King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visited injured passengers, while authorities and rail operators face pressure to explain what happened and identify safeguards. The investigation will need to establish responsibility from evidence rather than speculation as families wait for answers.

title: Enugu’s Coal City Games preparations enter technical review
excerpt: National Sports Commission and festival organisers scheduled venue inspections and technical meetings this week ahead of the November 27 opening of the 2026 National Sports Festival.
body: Preparations for the 23rd National Sports Festival in Enugu moved into a technical review this week, with the National Sports Commission and local organisers scheduled to inspect venues and meet from October 27 to 30. The event, branded the Coal City Games, is due to run from November 27 to December 11, 2026.

The Commission said the exercise was intended to assess facilities, review technical arrangements and identify issues that may need attention before athletes arrive. Participants were expected to include members of the Main Organising Committee, national sports federations, state sports directors, zonal coordinators and media representatives. The Commission’s published schedule set aside time for arrivals, venue inspections, a joint technical meeting and departures.

The review is an important checkpoint, but a scheduled inspection is not itself confirmation that every venue or support service is ready. Organisers still need to coordinate accommodation, transport, safety, medical support and competition operations across the host city. The festival will bring athletes from states and the Federal Capital Territory together, and its success will be measured both by the event itself and by the value of any sports facilities and skills it leaves in Enugu afterwards.

title: Nigeria and China sign $30 million grant agreement for community projects
excerpt: The 200 million yuan grant is intended for mutually agreed development projects. Nigerian officials say project proposals from states are being identified; a final list has not yet been announced.
body: Nigeria and China have signed a 200 million yuan grant agreement, valued at about US$30 million, to support development projects intended to benefit communities across Nigeria. The agreement was signed in Abuja by Nigeria’s Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Abubakar Bagudu, and Chinese Ambassador Yu Dunhai.

The two governments described the proposed work as small-scale projects designed to deliver practical benefits. Bagudu said the ministry and the Nigeria–China strategic partnership office were identifying proposals put forward by state governments. Officials have not yet published a final list of projects, locations, timelines or a detailed spending plan, so the specific communities and services that will benefit remain to be confirmed.

The grant comes as the countries mark 55 years of diplomatic relations and continue cooperation under a wider strategic partnership. The key test will be how the funding is translated into completed work and whether communities can see and verify the results. Transparent project selection, public reporting on expenditure and maintenance plans will help residents understand what the agreement delivers beyond the signing ceremony.

title: South Africa’s economy measures 4.9% larger after GDP revision
excerpt: Statistics South Africa’s rebasing raised its estimate of 2022 GDP to 6.99 trillion rand from 6.67 trillion rand, reflecting updated methods and data—not a sudden increase in production.
body: Statistics South Africa has revised the measured size of the country’s economy upward by 4.9 per cent for 2022, lifting the estimate from 6.67 trillion rand to 6.99 trillion rand. The update followed a rebasing and benchmarking exercise that changed the reference year for gross domestic product estimates from 2015 to 2022 and incorporated newer data and methods.

The statistical agency said the revision reflects a more complete picture of economic activity, including better measurement of parts of the non-observed economy. Mining, finance and trade recorded some of the largest changes. All ten industry groups tracked by the agency showed higher output under the revised series.

The revision does not mean that South Africa suddenly produced 4.9 per cent more goods and services in 2022. It is a change to the way past activity is measured. Rebasing matters because GDP is used to assess the scale and structure of the economy and calculate indicators such as public debt relative to GDP. It does not by itself show that household incomes, employment or living standards improved. Those outcomes require separate evidence.

title: Israel election leaves parliament without a clear governing majority
excerpt: Final results give Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc 53 seats, the main opposition 48 and Arab-led parties 19 in the 120-seat Knesset. Coalition talks will determine who can govern.
body: Final results from Israel’s parliamentary election have left no political bloc with the 61 seats needed for a majority in the 120-member Knesset. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc won 53 seats, the main opposition grouping led by Gadi Eisenkot won 48, and Arab-led parties secured 19 seats, according to the published count.

The result sets the stage for negotiations among parties with sharply different positions. The Arab-led parties’ combined representation is their strongest showing to date, but it is not yet clear whether they will support an opposition-led government or what terms any agreement might involve. Netanyahu remains prime minister while the process of forming a government proceeds.

The election authority has said the vote was conducted lawfully. Allegations of widespread interference made by some political figures have not been substantiated. The next steps include consultations and an effort to assemble a coalition capable of commanding a majority. If no group can form a government, the country could face another election. Until negotiations conclude, the results mark a change in parliamentary arithmetic rather than an immediate change in government.

title: Enugu court sentences woman after baby is recovered and reunited with parents
excerpt: Police say a four-month-old boy taken at Emene market was recovered in Nkanu East and returned to his parents. The accused pleaded guilty and received concurrent sentences.
body: An Enugu Magistrate Court has sentenced a woman to two concurrent three-year prison terms after she pleaded guilty to conspiracy and child stealing, according to the Enugu State Police Command. Police said the case began on October 20 at Oye-Emene Market, where the four-month-old boy was taken while his mother was nearby.

The command said officers worked with the Amechi-Idodo Police Division and neighbourhood watch members to investigate and locate the child. Police reported that the baby was recovered in Nkanu East Local Government Area on October 24 and reunited with his parents. The woman was arraigned after the investigation concluded and was convicted on October 29. The child’s identity has not been published here to protect his privacy.

The Commissioner of Police commended the officers and community members involved and urged parents and guardians to remain vigilant and report missing-child cases promptly. The recovery and court outcome bring a resolution to this case, while also underscoring the importance of rapid reporting, coordinated local response and safeguards for children in public places.

title: Tinubu defends borrowing plans and points to infrastructure investment
excerpt: The president argues new loans should be judged by the projects and public value they deliver, citing highways, power upgrades and ports as investment priorities.
body: President Bola Tinubu has defended the Federal Government’s fresh borrowing plans in an essay responding to criticism from opposition leaders and other commentators. He argued that the key question is not simply how much the country borrows, but what the financing builds and what lasting value it creates.

Tinubu cited the Lagos–Calabar Coastal Highway, the Sokoto–Badagry Superhighway, the Trans-Sahara Superhighway, electricity-grid upgrades and modernisation of commercial ports among projects intended to connect economic regions and support production. He also said investments in healthcare, education and vocational training should accompany physical infrastructure. The administration says these investments are part of a longer-term ambition to expand the economy and create employment.

The president’s argument places the emphasis on delivery: projects must be completed, costs controlled and benefits felt by households and businesses. Borrowing still carries repayment obligations, so public scrutiny will focus on the terms of the loans, how funds are allocated and whether promised projects produce measurable results. The essay sets out the government’s rationale; it does not by itself establish that the proposed investments have been completed or that their expected benefits have been achieved.

title: UN report finds restoration underway across 252 million hectares
excerpt: A new assessment documents restoration work in 149 countries and more than one million related jobs, but says financing and progress need to grow sharply before 2030.
body: A United Nations assessment says ecosystem restoration is underway across 252 million hectares in 149 countries, supporting more than one million jobs. The report, produced by the Food and Agriculture Organization, the UN Environment Programme and the Convention on Biological Diversity secretariat, describes this as the largest documented restoration effort to date.

The documented area is still below the international ambition to restore about one billion hectares by 2030. Progress is uneven: the report records extensive land-restoration work, while restoration of freshwater, marine and coastal ecosystems is much more limited. It estimates that annual restoration finance would need to rise from US$64 billion to US$296 billion by 2030 to meet the scale of the challenge.

The report also points to potential benefits for biodiversity, climate resilience and livelihoods, while warning that restoration cannot compensate for continued damage to ecosystems. It calls for governments to address the causes of degradation and improve monitoring so projects deliver lasting results. For communities, restoration is not only a conservation issue: healthy soils, water systems and coastal areas underpin food production, health and local economies.

title: Nigeria’s Samson Adamu confirmed as CAF General Secretary
excerpt: Adamu’s confirmation makes him the first Nigerian to hold the substantive post in the Confederation of African Football’s 70-year history, following several roles in the organisation.
body: The Confederation of African Football has confirmed Nigerian football administrator Samson Adamu as its substantive General Secretary. The Nigeria Football Federation welcomed the decision, which makes Adamu the first Nigerian to hold the post in CAF’s 70-year history.

Adamu joined the Cairo-based organisation as Director of Competitions and later served as Director of Tournaments and Events. He had been acting General Secretary since March, after Véron Mosengo-Omba stepped down. The NFF said his experience in football administration and tournament operations would support the work ahead and pledged cooperation with him in his new role.

The General Secretary leads CAF’s day-to-day administrative operations and works with the confederation’s leadership and 54 member associations. The appointment places a Nigerian administrator in a senior position at the governing body for African football, which oversees continental competitions and development programmes. The secretariat supports competition operations, correspondence with associations and implementation of decisions made by CAF’s governing bodies. Adamu’s earlier work in tournaments gives him direct experience with those operational responsibilities. His immediate task will be to manage the secretariat’s work and support the delivery of CAF’s activities across the continent.
